rounds.text: Coral India Finance & Housing Ltd trades at a remarkably low valuation, sitting at a price-to-book ratio of 0.63x against a book value of ₹ 51.4 while priced at ₹ 32.4 [E2], and at an even cheaper 0.66x relative to a sector benchmark of 1.54x [E7]. This disconnect is further underscored by a modest P/E of 8.82x [E1] that stands in stark contrast to the broader sector benchmark P/E of 26.55x [E6]. Operational efficiency outstrips the wider industry, as demonstrated by a robust return on assets of 6.62% that dwarfs the sector benchmark of -104.7% [E8], alongside an ROCE of 8.2% that comfortably beats the sector benchmark of 4.47% [E10] and sector median of 7.2% [E78]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is actively expanding with Capital Work in Progress surging by 50.0% to reach ₹ 6 Cr by March 2026 [E40], signaling a tangible build-up phase for future growth. Profit growth is also beginning to outpace 1-year price growth by 17%, indicating that the business is starting to outperform current market expectations [E57]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted sharply over the trailing twelve months by -41% [E17] alongside a multi-year slowdown in top-line expansion [E14, E15, E16].

The business suffers from a profound, multi-year top-line contraction that undercuts any argument of structural health: compounded sales growth has slowed to 3% over 10 years [E14], worsened to -4% over 5 years [E15], dropped to -21% over 3 years [E16], and plunged catastrophically by -41% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. This severe revenue erosion aligns with an official negative flag noting poor sales growth of -4.49% over the past five years [E61], lagging far behind the sector median sales growth of 12.4% [E77]. Compounding these operational headwinds, the return profile remains persistently mediocre, evidenced by a low 3-year median ROE of 9% [E63] that further degraded to 7% over the last year [E29], triggering explicit screening warnings for low profitability and decelerating earnings growth [E70, E71]. Conceded: [E1] the stock trades at a low P/E of 8.82x alongside a price-to-book ratio of 0.63x [E2].

Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E16], [E17], [E29], [E61], [E63], [E70], [E71]. While top-line contraction is real, it completely ignores the massive valuation disconnect where the stock trades at a deep discount with a P/E of 8.82x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.63x [E2]. Furthermore, these multiples look extraordinarily cheap against sector benchmarks of 26.55x P/E and 1.54x P/B [E6, E7]. The company actually outperforms the broader sector on structural efficiency, generating an ROCE of 8.2% versus the sector benchmark of 4.47% [E10] and a superior ROA of 6.62% against a severely distressed sector benchmark of -104.7% [E8]. Additionally, capital allocation is actively pivoting toward future expansion, with Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) surging by +50.0% to Rs 6 Cr in March 2026 [E40]. Finally, fundamentals are already beginning to outpace market skepticism, as profit growth recently exceeds 1-year price growth by 17% [E57].

Conceded: [E6], [E7], [E8], [E10], [E40]. While the bull highlights sector comparisons and an increase in Capital Work-in-Progress to Rs 6 Cr [E40], these metrics do not override a severe structural decay in demand. Compounded sales growth has collapsed across every measurable horizon: down 3% over 10 years [E14], down 4% over 5 years [E15], down 21% over 3 years [E16], and plummeting by 41% in the trailing twelve months [E17]. This persistent contraction matches explicit negative operational flags [E61] and confirms that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E70]. Furthermore, the low price-to-book ratio of 0.63x [E2] is entirely justified by a depressed return on equity that has stagnated at a median of 9% over 10 and 3 years [E26, E28], falling further to just 7% over the last year [E29, E71]. A cheap multiple on a shrinking business is a classic value trap, not a margin of safety.
